# Layer 2 test evidence

All 151 tests of the Layer 2 SQL interface, by spec area. Each compiles a query and, almost always, runs it on DuckDB against a plain-SQL reference. A test named `s72_…` or `a2_…` follows that section or appendix of `relational_semantics.md`.

## Appendix A.1 and naming

Model-qualified relations, measure names, aliases and output labels, and what is not a Layer 2 query.

[`tests/sql_front/basics.rs`](https://github.com/lakeops-org/ossiec/blob/main/tests/sql_front/basics.rs) · 14 tests

|---|---|
| `model_qualified_relations_compile_the_same_as_bare_ones` | §11.2: a model's relations live in one schema named after the model, so `shop.orders` means the same as `orders`, in any part of the query. |
| `model_qualified_columns_work_in_a_view_body` | A view's body goes through the same names as a query. |
| `columns_qualified_by_another_schema_are_refused` | Only the model's own name qualifies a column. |
| `relations_outside_the_model_are_refused` |  |
| `a1_status_order_count_matches_layer3` |  |
| `qualified_measure_and_alias` |  |
| `measure_synonym_and_where` |  |
| `model_scoped_metric_is_refused` |  |
| `agg_of_expression_is_refused` |  |
| `consumer_aliases_name_output_columns` |  |
| `group_by_without_agg_equals_dimension_listing` |  |
| `nested_queries_are_not_layer3_requests` |  |
| `columns_are_named_as_in_standard_sql` | §3.1: columns behave as in standard SQL, named by their final part, and a relation's column names are unique. |
| `select_star_and_select_list_subqueries_are_refused_by_name` | `SELECT *` and a select-list subquery are refused by name, not as `AGG` arithmetic or a plain aggregate, which is what they would otherwise be read as. |

## Joins (§7.6, A.5, A.6)

Every kind, from either side, fan-out, and G2.

[`tests/sql_front/joins.rs`](https://github.com/lakeops-org/ossiec/blob/main/tests/sql_front/joins.rs) · 23 tests

| Test | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `inner_join_customers_emits_inner_join` |  |
| `left_join_customers_matches_layer3_agg_shape` |  |
| `right_join_keeps_customers_without_inflating_orders` |  |
| `full_join_keeps_both_sides_without_inflating_orders` |  |
| `cross_join_does_not_multiply_the_measure` |  |
| `cross_join_grouped_by_the_other_side_counts_each_order_once_per_group` |  |
| `comma_from_is_a_cross_join` | `FROM orders o, customers c` is `orders o CROSS JOIN customers c` (§7.6): the same SQL, and each order counted once per region. |
| `comma_from_before_a_left_join_keeps_its_meaning` | A comma binds looser than `JOIN`: `FROM c, o LEFT JOIN p ON …` is `c × (o LEFT JOIN p)`, which flattening to `c CROSS JOIN o LEFT JOIN p` keeps. |
| `comma_from_with_a_right_or_full_join_is_refused` | With a `RIGHT` or `FULL` join, `a, b RIGHT JOIN c` pairs `c`'s padded rows with every `a` row, which flattening can't express: refused, by name. |
| `cross_join_with_on_is_refused` |  |
| `derived_cross_join_does_not_multiply_the_measure` |  |
| `shell_right_and_cross_join_match_plain_sql` |  |
| `exotic_join_kind_is_still_refused` |  |
| `a5_unused_inner_join_customers_compiles` |  |
| `a5_reverse_fanout_join_uses_pk_dedup` |  |
| `a5_right_join_to_the_many_side_of_a_fanout_dedups` | `orders RIGHT JOIN order_items` keeps every line. |
| `join_from_either_side_without_a_fact_key` | Two-facts `orders` has no primary key, so null-extended customers are kept out of `SUM` by a FILTER on the join key rather than by de-duplication. |
| `join_from_the_one_side_filters_each_term_of_a_composite_metric` | A composite metric is planned as one aggregate per term, and each takes the FILTER: `COUNT(*)` counts no orders for a customer that has none, so its ratio is NULL rather than divided by the one null-extended row. |
| `join_from_the_one_side_filters_every_aggregate_shape` | Aggregates of every shape take the FILTER, ANDed with a FILTER of their own, so a fact without a primary key needs no de-duplication for any of them. |
| `right_joins_along_a_chain_without_a_fact_key` | orders -> customers -> regions, `orders` without a primary key. |
| `left_join_from_the_one_side_drops_unmatched_fact_rows` | §7.6, §8.1: `customers LEFT JOIN orders` keeps every customer and the orders that match one. |
| `join_kind_changes_the_request_hash` | The join kind is part of a query's identity: an `INNER` and a `LEFT` join compile to different SQL, so they must not share a `request_hash`. |
| `a_repeated_alias_is_refused_in_every_join_form` | One alias names one relation, however the second one is joined: a comma item, a `CROSS JOIN` or a relationship join. |

## Appendix A.4

Measures from independent facts, and the query as one relation (§7.6, §10.2).

[`tests/sql_front/multi_fact.rs`](https://github.com/lakeops-org/ossiec/blob/main/tests/sql_front/multi_fact.rs) · 12 tests

| Test | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `a4_independent_measures_via_joins_agree_with_layer3` | `customers LEFT JOIN orders LEFT JOIN tickets` keeps every customer, so customer 5 (no region, nothing bought) is a NULL-region group with no sales and no tickets. |
| `a4_comma_from_is_a_cross_join_not_independent_facts` | A comma `FROM` is a cross join, as in SQL (§7.6, §10.2), not a list of independent facts (those are written with joins, as A.4 does). |
| `a4_refuses_dimension_not_shared_across_facts` |  |
| `a4_agg_ratio_expression_in_select` |  |
| `a4_agg_ratio_on_single_fact` |  |
| `count_star_on_two_facts_stays_two_terms` | `COUNT(*)` on two facts is the same SQL over different rows: two terms, not one. |
| `joins_on_one_fact_narrow_the_other` | The query is one relation (§7.6, §10.2), however its facts are planned: a join that drops customers drops them for every measure. |
| `narrowing_across_facts_refuses_include_unmatched` | Narrowing across facts isn't implemented for `includeUnmatched`, whose unmatched rows would need it too: refused rather than answered wrongly. |
| `a2_derived_join_narrows_every_fact` | The query is one relation (§7.6, §10.2): the inner join to `d` keeps only the top two customers' rows (1 and 2, both EU), for every measure. |
| `a4_ratio_with_a_derived_join_on_one_fact` | The ratio over a relation the derived join narrows: only EU's top customers are in it, for orders and tickets alike (§7.6, §10.2): 60 / 3. |
| `a4_where_on_one_fact_narrows_the_other` | §7.3, §10.2: a `WHERE` on one fact's columns filters the one relation, so it keeps that fact's rows that pass and the customers that still have one; the other fact keeps only those customers' rows. |
| `a4_where_on_one_fact_refusals` | A predicate a padded row can pass, on one fact, keeps rows no leg has; and a predicate across both facts has no one leg to go on. |

## Query operators (§7.3–§7.8)

`WHERE`, `HAVING`, `ORDER BY`, `GROUP BY ALL`, `DISTINCT` and `WITH`.

[`tests/sql_front/operators.rs`](https://github.com/lakeops-org/ossiec/blob/main/tests/sql_front/operators.rs) · 10 tests

| Test | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `where_accepts_any_row_predicate` | §7.3: `WHERE` is an ordinary row predicate, on any column the query can read. |
| `having_keeps_or_drops_finished_groups` | §7.5: `HAVING` may contain `AGG()` and scalar expressions over it. |
| `with_names_derived_tables` | §7.7: a CTE is a derived table with a name. |
| `having_keeps_each_engines_rules` | What a target's SQL has to carry, which DuckDB's answers can't show. |
| `having_refuses_a_window_metric` | A window runs after HAVING, so one in a measure can't be compared there. |
| `order_by_reads_measures_that_are_not_selected` | §7.5: `ORDER BY` may contain `AGG()` and scalar expressions over it. |
| `group_by_all_groups_by_the_selected_fields` | §7.4: `GROUP BY ALL` is the list of selected non-aggregates. |
| `distinct_keeps_one_of_each_row` | §7.8: `DISTINCT` is valid over fields and evaluated measures. |
| `distinct_refuses_unevaluated_measures` | §7.8: an unevaluated measure has no value to compare. |
| `having_and_order_by_read_plain_aggregates` | §7.2, §7.5: a plain aggregate in `HAVING` or `ORDER BY` reads the group's joined rows as plain SQL does, beside `AGG()`, whether or not it is selected. |
